audit.whatIsWrong: Both layers call Sylas's E a stun: the full layer's dosFull[0] said 'His dash + stun (recast pull)' and the content layer says 'E chain-dash stun' in spikes[0], whys[1] and early.
audit.why: Abscond / Abduct is a dash whose recast throws chains and pulls Sylas to the enemy hit — Riot's description contains no stun, and the derived kit flags for that slot are projectile + dash only, with no hardCC (compare Swain's Nevermove and Urgot's Disdain, both of which do carry hardCC). Telling a Nasus he is about to be stunned changes whether he holds Wither or Flash, so the error is not cosmetic.
audit.corrected: It is a dash out with a recast chain-pull in, not a stun. Both halves share one cooldown: 13/12/11/10/9s.
sources: champ-data/_kits/sylas.json — E Abscond / Abduct description and flags
champ-data/_kits/swain.json and urgot.json — hardCC flag present on genuine CC slots

audit.whatIsWrong: The content layer repeatedly calls Chain Lash a 'Q drain' (spikes[0], whys[1], whys[3], early, mid).
audit.why: Chain Lash damages and slows and then detonates after a delay. It does not heal him. Kingslayer is the heal. Attributing the sustain to the wrong spell sends the player to bait the wrong cooldown.
audit.corrected: Chain Lash is the slow-and-detonate poke (10/9/8/7/6s); Kingslayer is the healing lunge (12/10.5/9/7.5/6s).
sources: champ-data/_kits/sylas.json — Q Chain Lash and W Kingslayer descriptions

audit.whatIsWrong: The full layer never mentions Hijack. Its matchup-defining cooldown, its dos, its donts and its level-6 phase all point at Abscond / Abduct instead.
audit.why: Hijack copies Fury of the Sands. A Nasus who opens the all-in with his ultimate hands Sylas the same bonus health, resists, damage aura and reduced Q cooldown he just used. That single fact decides the level-6 fight and it was only in the content layer.
audit.corrected: Level 6 phase and the cooldown section now lead with Hijack at 80/55/30s: never open with R.
sources: champ-data/_kits/nasus.json — R Fury of the Sands

audit.whatIsWrong: The full layer gave Sylas stages 1-5; the content chart gives him only stages 2 and 4 with the rest Skill.
audit.why: Nasus wins 49.93% over 1390 games — the largest sample in this slice and a genuinely even lane. Five straight enemy-favoured stages does not describe an even matchup.
audit.corrected: phases[0], [2] and [4] moved to Skill to match the content chart; stages 2 and 4 left with Sylas.

audit.whatIsWrong: No anti-heal called anywhere despite Kingslayer being his sustain through every extended trade.
audit.why: Kingslayer heals him against champions on a cooldown that falls to 6s. Nasus wins by grinding; Sylas wins by out-healing the grind.
audit.corrected: Grievous Wounds now named in dontsFull[1] and whys[3].

edits.before: Q start, last-hit only. Sylas wins every level-1 exchange — concede the bush, concede the trades, take the stacks.
edits.after: Q start, last-hit only. Nobody wins level 1 here — Sylas has one spell up, so deny his last-hits and bank stacks.

edits.before: E lets you stack safely from range when Sylas zones you. Spirit Fire the wave under tower; every stack denied is his only real win condition.
edits.after: Wither is online. Abscond is a 13s dash at rank 1 and the chain-pull recast shares it — once he spends it to close, he has no exit from your Q range.

edits.before: Fury of the Sands flips dives: pop R, Wither Sylas, and suddenly the stat-check runs your way. First real fight you're allowed to take.
edits.after: Hijack steals Fury of the Sands — if you ult first he gets a copy of it. Bait it or hold R; his ult is only 80s at rank 1.

edits.before: - Sylas Abscond / Abduct: matchup-defining — His dash + stun (recast pull). Bait it, then commit. Track it before every engage.
edits.after: - Sylas Hijack: 80/55/30s — it copies your Fury of the Sands, so never open with R. - Sylas Abscond: 13/12/11/10/9s — his only exit.

edits.before: His dash + stun (recast pull). Bait it, then commit. Only engage once it is down or baited.
edits.after: His dash out and his chain-pull back in share one 13s cooldown — bait it, then commit.

edits.before: Sylas wastes Abscond / Abduct — commit the full pattern immediately.
edits.after: Withered, he cannot reposition between Chain Lash detonations.

edits.before: Burning your answer for tiny value leaves you naked for its full cooldown.
edits.after: Kingslayer heals him off you — Grievous Wounds before any extended trade.

edits.before: Sylas spikes first — his E chain-dash stun plus Q drain lets him poke your stacking and bully you off Siphoning Strike farm.
edits.after: Sylas spikes first — Abscond's chain-pull plus Kingslayer's heal lets him poke your stacking and bully you off Siphoning Strike farm.

edits.before: Sylas spikes with E's chain-dash stun and Q drain, bullying you off stacks before you have Wither to answer.
edits.after: Sylas spikes with Abscond's chain-pull and Kingslayer's heal, bullying you off stacks before you have Wither.

edits.before: He out-pokes a stack-hungry Nasus through 4-5 — his Q drain plus W sustain beats your lifesteal while you're farming not trading.
edits.after: He out-pokes you through 4-5 — Chain Lash plus Kingslayer's heal beats your lifesteal unless you already hold Grievous Wounds.
